description: pysheds is Matt Bartos and contributors' Python library for deriving drainage structure from digital elevation models. It conditions terrain by filling pits and depressions and resolving flats, then calculates flow directions, accumulation, catchment boundaries, river networks and distances to outlets. Inputs are elevation rasters and selected pour points; outputs include raster fields and extracted river geometry. Geographic coverage follows the input terrain, with spatial resolution inherited from its grid, not a fixed global product. Public source and package installation are free under GPL-3.0. A limitation is that catchments depend on DEM quality, conditioning choices and routing assumptions; the README's performance figures describe particular grids and hardware. The examples cover D8 and other routing schemes and provide raster and ASCII output functions. pysheds can prepare catchments and flow paths for drainage or flood simulations alongside Delft3D FM (model-delft3d-fm). Its software citation is the repository's 2020 Zenodo release. No elevation raster or example archive was downloaded.
